ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How do you read the syllable سِ? (1 mark)
   A. si
   B. mu
   C. laa
   D. tu

2. Which letter has three dots above it? (1 mark)
   A. ث (thaa)
   B. ت (taa)
   C. ب (baa)
   D. ج (jiim)

3. How is the Arabic word ابْنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. khaal
   B. ʿamma
   C. jadd
   D. ibn

4. How do you read the syllable لَا? (1 mark)
   A. du
   B. bii
   C. si
   D. laa

5. In a passage about the home, which of these is a theme word? (1 mark)
   A. al-ahad
   B. kursii (chair)
   C. shukran
   D. marhaban

6. Which Arabic word means "lamp"? (1 mark)
   A. كُرْسِيٌّ
   B. غُرْفَةٌ
   C. مِصْبَاحٌ
   D. خِزَانَةٌ

7. What does the word ghadan mean? (1 mark)
   A. week
   B. today
   C. tomorrow
   D. yesterday

8. Which day name comes from the Arabic word for 'one'? (1 mark)
   A. al-khamiis
   B. as-sabt
   C. al-jumuʿa
   D. al-ahad

9. Which Arabic word means "Saturday"? (1 mark)
   A. الْجُمُعَةُ
   B. الْيَوْمَ
   C. الْأَرْبِعَاءُ
   D. السَّبْتُ

10. How is the Arabic word دَوْرُكَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. dawruka
   B. ʿasiir
   C. kaʿka
   D. mabruuk

11. How is the Arabic word أُغْنِيَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. shamʿa
   B. sharaab
   C. taʿaam
   D. ughniya

12. What does the Arabic sentence هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The friends are at the party.
   B. Above the table there is a balloon.
   C. This is a party.
   D. On the table there is a cake.

13. How is the Arabic word دَجَاجٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. bayd
   B. sukkar
   C. dajaaj
   D. aruzz

14. Which Arabic word means "eggs"? (1 mark)
   A. ذُرَةٌ
   B. لَحْمٌ
   C. جَزَرٌ
   D. بَيْضٌ

15. How is the Arabic word بَطْنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. raʾs
   B. jism
   C. rijl
   D. batn

16. Which Arabic word means "head"? (1 mark)
   A. رَأْسٌ
   B. أُذُنٌ
   C. فَمٌ
   D. سِنٌّ

17. Which Arabic word means "river"? (1 mark)
   A. شَمْسٌ
   B. نَهْرٌ
   C. مَطَرٌ
   D. سَمَاءٌ

18. How is the Arabic word حَارٌّ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. matar
   B. shajara
   C. haarr
   D. shams

19. Which Arabic word means "window"? (1 mark)
   A. نَافِذَةٌ
   B. طَاوِلَةٌ
   C. مِصْبَاحٌ
   D. غُرْفَةٌ

20. Which Arabic word means "key"? (1 mark)
   A. كُوبٌ
   B. حَمَّامٌ
   C. خِزَانَةٌ
   D. مِفْتَاحٌ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how a spelling bee is played. (3 marks) (3 marks)

22. Describe the steps of making a class picture book on family celebrations. (4 marks) (4 marks)

23. Translate into English: jaddii kabiir (2 marks)

24. Translate into English: ash-shamsu fii s-samaa'i (2 marks)

25. Write in Arabic sounds a question and an answer about bananas and give the meaning. (4 marks) (4 marks)

26. List four theme words about the home in Arabic (English letters), with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

27. Explain what pace is and describe a good pace for reading aloud. (3 marks) (3 marks)

28. Give three differences between the Arabic and the English alphabets. (3 marks) (3 marks)

29. Translate into English: haadhaa jismii (2 marks)

30. Give three examples of non-verbal cues you could use when reciting a poem about weather. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — si
   سِ is read si.

2. A — ث (thaa)
   Thaa has three dots above. Baa has one dot below and taa has two dots above.

3. D — ibn
   ابْنٌ is read ibn and means son.

4. D — laa
   لَا is read laa.

5. B — kursii (chair)
   A theme word belongs to the topic. A chair is found in the home.

6. C — مِصْبَاحٌ
   مِصْبَاحٌ (misbaah) means lamp.

7. C — tomorrow
   ghadan means tomorrow. amsi means yesterday.

8. D — al-ahad
   al-ahad, Sunday, is the first day.

9. D — السَّبْتُ
   السَّبْتُ (as-sabt) means Saturday.

10. A — dawruka
   دَوْرُكَ is read dawruka and means your turn.

11. D — ughniya
   أُغْنِيَةٌ is read ughniya and means song.

12. C — This is a party.
   هَذِهِ حَفْلَةٌ (haadhihi hafla) means: This is a party.

13. C — dajaaj
   دَجَاجٌ is read dajaaj and means chicken.

14. D — بَيْضٌ
   بَيْضٌ (bayd) means eggs.

15. D — batn
   بَطْنٌ is read batn and means stomach.

16. A — رَأْسٌ
   رَأْسٌ (raʾs) means head.

17. B — نَهْرٌ
   نَهْرٌ (nahr) means river.

18. C — haarr
   حَارٌّ is read haarr and means hot.

19. A — نَافِذَةٌ
   نَافِذَةٌ (naafidha) means window.

20. D — مِفْتَاحٌ
   مِفْتَاحٌ (miftaah) means key.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Teams take turns; a learner says the Arabic word and spells it by naming the letters; correct spelling earns a point.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for teams, 1 mark for spelling by letter names and 1 mark for scoring.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect or draw pictures of celebration things; put one on each page; write an Arabic word or sentence with the meaning; make a cover with a title.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: My grandfather is old (big in age).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun is in the sky.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: hal tuhibbu l-mawz? naʿam, uhibbu l-mawz. Do you like bananas? Yes, I like bananas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for each meaning.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example bayt (house), matbakh (kitchen), taawila (table), kursii (chair).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pace is the speed of reading. A good pace is steady, not too fast so that listeners understand, and not so slow that the sentence sounds broken.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 2 marks for the description.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Arabic is read from right to left; it has no capital letters; letters join and change shape; it uses marks for short vowels; it has sounds like ʿayn and Haa that English does not have.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference, up to 3.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lifting arms for the sun; wiggling fingers downwards for rain; smiling at the last line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cue that matches a word.
